justifications.functional_suitability: The architecture satisfies all requirements: R-01 is explicitly addressed by Catalog Management Component (handling physical/digital items) and Catalog UI Module. Circulation & Fines Component and Circulation Module support circulation workflows and self-service portals.
justifications.performance_efficiency: Target R-05 (<800 ms search) is supported by a dedicated Search Service backed by Elasticsearch, PgBouncer Connection Pooler, PostgreSQL Read Replicas with pg_trgm, and asynchronous decoupling via Message Broker.
justifications.compatibility: Interoperability is well handled using open standards: OIDC for Identity Provider, REST via OpenFeign for National Library Registry, AMQP for Message Broker, and HTTPS for Payment Gateway and Notification Service.
justifications.usability: The React/TypeScript Web Application accommodates both Library Patrons and Library Staff via Router Component, Catalog UI Module, and Circulation Module, though distinct user journeys or specialized accessibility mechanisms are not explicitly detailed.
justifications.reliability: Fault tolerance is thoroughly addressed via Circuit Breaker Component (Resilience4j) protecting search endpoints, Retry Coordinator with exponential backoff, Dead Letter Handler for poison messages, and PostgreSQL Read Replicas.
justifications.security: The EU-only residency constraint is enforced across Database, Message Broker Data Policy Enforcement Component, and pinned external services. Security includes JWT Validation Filter, Spring Security context validation, and pgAudit subsystem.
justifications.maintainability: The system exhibits high modularity with clear separation of concerns across Core Domain Service, Search Service, and Notification Worker, paired with event-driven loose coupling via RabbitMQ/Kafka and Spring Cloud components.
justifications.portability: Cloud-hosted SaaS containers (Spring Boot, Node.js, React SPA) and standard infrastructure (PostgreSQL, Elasticsearch) allow portability across cloud vendors, though deployment manifests or container orchestration specifics are omitted.

PERF-01.justification: A dedicated Search Service using Elasticsearch and connection-pooled replicas handles high-concurrency queries behind a reactive API Gateway. However, an explicit caching layer is omitted.
sensitivity_points: Elasticsearch query execution efficiency under high load
tradeoffs: Elasticsearch cluster resource overhead versus sub-second read latency

PERF-02.justification: CQRS separation decouples writes from searches. Catalog updates are published asynchronously to the Message Broker and consumed by the Search Service, easily achieving propagation within five minutes.
sensitivity_points: Message broker delivery latency for item updates
tradeoffs: Eventual consistency of catalog updates versus zero impact on search performance

AVAIL-01.justification: Circulation is completely isolated in the Core Domain Service and Database. The API Gateway circuit breaker protects downstream services from search index node failure, preventing lost loans.
sensitivity_points: Decoupling of circulation transactions from search cluster health
tradeoffs: Temporary degradation of search functionality versus continuous loan processing availability

AVAIL-02.justification: The SPA front end on CDN alongside stateless API Gateway and Core Domain Service instances allows immediate traffic failover to healthy replicas without interrupting active loan transactions.
sensitivity_points: Session state independence across client and gateway instances
Database ACID transaction rollback guarantees during node failure
tradeoffs: Stateless service design overhead versus simplified failover resilience

MOD-01.justification: The architecture includes a specific National Library Registry integration but lacks an extensible adapter pattern or plugin interface in the Core Domain Service for third-party e-book providers.
sensitivity_points: Coupling of catalog domain logic to external provider protocols
tradeoffs: Monolithic domain component simplicity versus modular provider extensibility

MOD-02.justification: Circulation and loan rules are embedded in the Spring Boot Circulation & Fines Component without a dynamic configuration store or business rules engine to alter policies at runtime without redeployment.
sensitivity_points: Embedding policy rules within compiled application code
tradeoffs: Development speed of embedded rules versus zero-downtime policy configuration flexibility

SEC-01.justification: Data residency constraints are explicitly enforced at all tiers: databases, brokers, and external systems are strictly pinned to EU endpoints, reinforced by gateway query sanitization.
sensitivity_points: Strict regional pinning of all third-party integration endpoints
tradeoffs: Strict EU data residency compliance versus freedom in vendor service selection

SEC-02.justification: API Gateway token validation paired with Spring Security context checks enforces patron-level authorization, while pgAudit and the audit message queue reliably record unauthorized access attempts.
sensitivity_points: Enforcement of tenant and patron record boundaries in domain logic
tradeoffs: Comprehensive audit trail overhead versus patron data confidentiality
